audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart says 'Skill' on rows 1, 4-5 and First item while content, packet and prose all say Swain owns every stage until two items.
audit.why: Kassadin is among the weakest level-1 laners, has only the 9s Null Sphere shield to defend trades pre-6, and only flips the matchup at two-plus items with stacked Riftwalk.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side, phases[3].side and phases[5].side moved to Swain with rewritten whys and ratings.

audit.why: Spikes correctly frame your pre-6 dominance, your 6 window, the first-item clock, and his two-item takeover.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldowns field had no numbers; the Nether Blade auto-reset burst tell (flagged missing interaction) was absent; do/don't bullets were pasted trade lines.
audit.why: Null Sphere's shield is 9s at rank 1 and is his only trade defence pre-6; Riftwalk is 5s but doubles in mana cost per stack; his combo opens with the W auto reset — the wind-up is the step-back cue.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and the mana-stack note in breakdown.cooldowns; W-reset tell in dontsFull[2].d; W-scouting body under the roam-timer title.

audit.whatIsWrong: The _missing list claims Null Sphere is a channel that Nevermove cancels.
audit.why: Riot's text says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels; the 'channel' derived flag looks like a tooltip-parse misfire, so the claim is not written to the page.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving lane, stacking items, then Riftwalk-bursting your carries faster than your R heals.

edits.before: Ahead, become the map: W every objective setup, root every contest, and ascend into fights Kassadin has to take — the drain converts leads into inevitabilities.
edits.after: Ahead, spend the lead before he scales: W every objective, root every contest, and end — a Kassadin behind on levels never reaches the two-item flip.

edits.before: Q-poke through the wave — the hand hurts more than people remember. Farm safely; your real spells arrive next.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest level-1 laners — Q-poke him off the wave freely; he has only W autos to answer you.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-spam stops costing the lane. Poke the wave contact and pull every rooted target with the passive.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you deny the CS and XP his whole game depends on — Lost Chapter funds Q-spam and he still cannot trade back.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: the drain outpaces their damage in any extended fight. Force rivers, root the entry, ascend, profit.
edits.after: First item you are still ahead — convert tempo into roams and plates; every lead here is a down-payment on his flip.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared slow push with W covering the river — your shove funds vision, and rooted gank targets pay double. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower against artillery — every last-hit is a free poke window for him and a long rootless walk for you. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: a Q-cleared slow push with W covering the river — your shove funds vision, and rooted gank targets pay double. Worst wave: letting it freeze on his side — safe last-hits are exactly the quiet scaling he wants, and you cannot punish across it. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. It governs your forward steps. - E Nevermove spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Null Sphere's magic shield is 9s at rank 1 — his only trade defence pre-6; walk up and E-Q while it's down. - Riftwalk is 5s but mana-gated: each stack doubles the cost, so a chase runs him dry. - Your 12s E spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: E his step-up, passive-pull the root for the chunk + heal, Q the retreat — every landed root is a won trade with a health refund attached.
edits.after: Riftwalk roams are fast and quiet — a 7000-range W on his likely path turns his bot-lane dive into a ping your team sees coming.

edits.before: Brawling pre-6 like the demon is already online — Swain without R is a slow mage with a dream and a root on cooldown.
edits.after: His combo opens with the Nether Blade auto reset — the wind-up is your cue to step back and root the exit, not to follow him in.

notes: Chart rows 1, 4-5 and First item moved from 'Skill' to Swain to agree with content win[] and the packet (win[N] already agreed, so side edited alone per the chart rule).
